name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
short_status: Success: landed in Le Monnier crater on 15 January 1973; Lunokhod 2 drove about 39 km over four lunar days, an off-world distance record that stood until 2014, and its French-built reflector is still ranged from Earth.
tagline: Soviet Union · Rover · 1973 · The space race Success
stats: driven over four lunar days (37 km official odometry, 39.16 km on the LROC remap)
operated before dust on the radiator overheated it
year Opportunity on Mars finally broke its off-world driving record
1993 Sotheby's price for the derelict rover and its lander

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 8 January 1973, 06:55:38 UTC, Proton-K/D from Baikonur Cosmodrome (Tyuratam)

facts.label: Lunar orbit
facts.value: 12 January 1973, braked into a 90 x 100 km lunar orbit at 60 degrees inclination

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 15 January 1973, 23:35 UT, Le Monnier crater on the eastern edge of Mare Serenitatis, about 170 km north of the Apollo 17 site; Lunokhod 2 rolled down the ramps at 01:14 UT on 16 January

facts.label: LROC-derived coordinates
facts.value: Luna 21 lander at 26.005 N, 30.406 E; Lunokhod 2 final parking position at 25.830 N, 30.914 E

facts.label: Rover
facts.value: 840 kg, about 170 cm long, 160 cm wide and 135 cm high, eight independently driven wheels, riding a hinged solar lid

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: Three navigation TV cameras plus four panoramic telephotometers, a soil-mechanics penetrometer, RIFMA X-ray fluorescence spectrometer, magnetometer, astrophotometer, and a French-built laser corner-cube retroreflector

facts.label: Data return
facts.value: 86 panoramas and more than 80,000 TV pictures, plus magnetometer and soil-mechanics measurements along the traverse

facts.label: Traverse
facts.value: 37 km by the original mission odometry; the LROC-based cartography of Karachevtseva et al. (2017), tracing the tracks in NAC images, measured the full route at 39.16 km

facts.label: Distance record
facts.value: Held the off-world driving record until NASA's Opportunity rover passed 40 km on Mars on 27 July 2014

facts.label: End of mission
facts.value: 9 May 1973: the open lid touched a crater wall and dumped dust onto the radiator; the internal temperature then climbed to about 47 C, contact was lost on 10 May, and TASS announced the mission over on 3 June 1973

facts.label: Laser retroreflector
facts.value: French corner-cube array; unlike Lunokhod 1 its position was never lost, and after decades of weak green returns the Grasse station recovered near-full efficiency in infrared in 2015 to 2016

facts.label: Legal sale
facts.value: December 1993: the Lavochkin Association sold the Luna 21 lander and Lunokhod 2 rover for $68,500 at a Sotheby's auction in New York; the buyer was Richard Garriott

timeline: Braked into a 90 x 100 km lunar orbit
23:35 UT: Luna 21 soft-lands on the floor of Le Monnier crater
01:14 UT: Lunokhod 2 rolls down the ramps and begins driving
The open lid brushes a crater wall and dumps insulating dust onto the radiator
Overheating found on the 503rd session, near 47 C inside; contact is lost
TASS announces the mission is over after about four lunar days of driving
Lavochkin sells the Luna 21 lander and Lunokhod 2 rover at Sotheby's to Richard Garriott for $68,500
LROC images Lunokhod 2 parked with its lid open, tracks running north across Le Monnier
Opportunity on Mars passes 40 km, ending Lunokhod 2's 41-year off-world driving record
Karachevtseva et al. remap the full traverse from LROC images at 39.16 km, above the 37 km mission figure
